# StudentPay: Buy Now Pay Later for College Students

**Lender:** Kaveri Finance Ltd (NBFC). **Platform:** StudentPay app, operated by EduTech Labs Pvt Ltd as Lending Service Provider.

## 1. Product overview
StudentPay lets college students buy laptops, course material and coaching subscriptions and repay in 3, 6 or 9 monthly instalments. Credit limits start at ₹5,000 and go up to ₹40,000.

## 2. Onboarding and KYC
Students sign up with their mobile number and complete video KYC. During KYC the app asks once for camera and microphone access, with an explicit consent screen explaining why. We collect age, college name, course, and the student's monthly allowance or stipend as income details.

## 3. Smarter credit scoring
To approve students with thin credit files, the app reads the phone's contact list and call logs in the background and checks how many contacts are already StudentPay customers. Students with many repaying friends get a higher limit.

## 4. Credit limit growth
Every three months, if the student has repaid on time, the app automatically raises their credit limit by 25% and sends a congratulations notification. No action is needed from the student.

## 5. Disbursal
For course fees, the loan amount is paid directly into the bank account of the college or coaching institute. For laptops, the amount goes directly to the merchant's bank account at checkout.

## 6. Repayment
Students repay through UPI autopay mandates set up on Kaveri Finance's own collection account. Statements, the KFS and the sanction letter are emailed and sent by SMS automatically as soon as the loan is booked.

## 7. Grievances
Kaveri Finance and EduTech Labs have each appointed a nodal grievance redressal officer, whose name, email and phone number are shown on the app's Help screen, on both websites and in the KFS.

Qwen3 8B.summary: The compliance review of the StudentPay product identified multiple violations against the RBI rules. The product feature does not provide borrowers with the option to give or deny consent for data usage, which violates DLD2025:12(ii). The 'Smarter credit scoring' feature accesses mobile phone resources without explicit consent, violating DLD2025:12(i). The 'Credit Limit Growth' feature automatically increases credit limits without explicit borrower request, violating DLD2025:7(ii). Disbursal to third-party accounts, including college and merchant accounts, is prohibited unless justified, violating DLD2025:9(i). The feature does not ensure all required digitally signed documents are automatically sent to the borrower, violating DLD2025:8(iii). Lastly, repayments through a third-party collection account violate the requirement for direct repayment into the RE’s bank account, violating DLD2025:9(ii).

# QuickCash: Instant Salary Advance

**Lender:** Sahyadri Capital (NBFC). **Platform:** QuickCash app by QC Technologies (LSP).

## 1. What it is
Salaried users can borrow ₹2,000 to ₹50,000 for 7 to 60 days, repaid in one shot on salary day.

## 2. Pricing
Interest is charged at 2.5% per month. QuickCash also charges the borrower a platform fee of 3% of the loan amount, collected by QC Technologies from the borrower's account at disbursal, for the use of the app.

## 3. Disbursal flow
Approved amounts are first credited to the QuickCash wallet held by QC Technologies, and the user can move the money to their bank account at any time with one tap.

## 4. Loan offer and KFS
After approval the user sees the Key Facts Statement with the APR, repayment schedule and all charges. For speed, the offer and KFS expire 30 minutes after they are shown; after that the user must apply again.

## 5. Cooling-off
Borrowers can cancel the loan within 3 days by repaying the principal and proportionate interest. A one-time processing fee of ₹99, which is shown in the KFS, is retained on cancellation.

## 6. Data
All app data is stored on AWS Mumbai region servers. QC Technologies keeps only the borrower's name, address and phone number, which it needs to service the loan; all other data sits with Sahyadri Capital.

# LoanBazaar: Personal Loan Marketplace

**Platform:** LoanBazaar, an LSP with agreements with six lenders (two banks and four NBFCs).

## 1. How matching works
The borrower enters amount, tenor, income and city. LoanBazaar sends the request to all six lenders and shows the offers that match the borrower's needs.

## 2. Offer screen
Offers are shown as cards with the lender name, loan amount, tenor and EMI. To keep the screen simple, the APR and penal charges are not shown on the card; borrowers can find them in the KFS after they choose an offer. Lenders that did not make an offer are not listed.

## 3. Recommended lender
The offer from FastLend NBFC, which pays LoanBazaar the highest commission, is pinned at the top with a "Best for you" badge and is pre-selected, so the borrower only has to press Continue.

## 4. Consistency
The matching rules are written down in an internal policy, and every change is versioned and approved by LoanBazaar's risk committee. The same rules apply to all borrowers with the same profile.

## 5. Website disclosures
Each lender's website lists LoanBazaar as an LSP, describes what LoanBazaar does for it, and links to the RBI Complaint Management System and Sachet portal. LoanBazaar's app links to each lender's website.

(4) The feature does not explicitly mention a link to the RE’s website, which is a requirement under DLD2025:17(iv), and is also a high-risk issue. (5) While the feature links to the RBI Complaint Management System and Sachet Portal, it does not explicitly mention the RE’s own website, which is a medium-risk issue. Overall, the product has multiple compliance gaps that require immediate attention.

**Lender:** Godavari Rural Bank. **Platform:** KisanFlex app by AgriNext Solutions (LSP).

Farmers get short-term credit of ₹10,000 to ₹1,50,000 to buy seeds, fertiliser and pesticide from partner agri-input dealers, repayable after harvest.

Credit is paid directly into the bank account of the agri-input dealer when the farmer buys inputs, against an invoice uploaded in the app.

To make repayment easy in villages, farmers repay into a pooled collection account run by AgriNext, which sweeps the money to Godavari Rural Bank every Friday.

For overdue loans, AgriNext field agents may collect cash from farmers. Cash collected is deposited and credited to the farmer's loan account within seven working days. AgriNext deducts its 5% recovery fee from the cash collected before depositing the rest.

When a loan becomes overdue, the assigned recovery agent visits the farmer. The farmer receives the agent's name and ID card details by SMS before the first visit.

## 6. Credit bureau reporting
All loans, irrespective of tenor or amount, are reported by Godavari Rural Bank to all four credit information companies every month.

Unsecured personal loans of ₹20,000 to ₹3,00,000 for 6 to 36 months.

To make login fast and secure, FaceFin stores each customer's face template and fingerprint data on its servers and uses them for every login and loan approval.

A full privacy policy is published on the website and in the app, listing the third parties that collect data through the app and the data storage, retention and destruction rules.

Before every loan we collect and keep on record the borrower's age, occupation, employer and monthly income from salary slips.

# ShopEase PayLater: Checkout Financing for E-commerce

**Lender:** Coastal Finance (NBFC). **Platform:** ShopEase PayLater, run by ShopEase Commerce Pvt Ltd (LSP).

## 1. Product
Shoppers can split purchases of ₹1,000 to ₹25,000 into 3 interest-free monthly payments. ShopEase earns a merchant discount from sellers.

Because these are small, short-term deferred payments, Coastal Finance does not report them to credit information companies. Only loans above ₹25,000 or longer than 6 months are reported.

There is no interest. A late payment fee of ₹250 is shown in the KFS. ShopEase later plans to add a monthly "account maintenance fee" of ₹49 for active users; this is not in the KFS and will be added to the bill automatically.

App store listing and ads say: "ShopEase PayLater: an RBI-approved credit app." ShopEase is listed on the RBI CIMS portal by Coastal Finance.

## 5. Cooling-off
Shoppers who change their mind can cancel within 2 days of purchase by paying back the principal with no extra charge.

## 6. Data sharing
Purchase and repayment history is shared with ShopEase's advertising partners to show personalised offers. Users are not asked separately; this is covered by accepting the app's terms of use.

**Regulated entity:** Coastal Finance (NBFC). **Partner:** CredBridge Technologies Pvt Ltd (LSP, incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013).

CredBridge sources personal loans of ₹25,000 to ₹2,00,000 for Coastal Finance and provides a default loss guarantee (DLG) on the portfolio.

CredBridge will cover losses up to 10% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio.

The DLG will be given as a corporate guarantee from CredBridge's parent company, rather than cash or a bank guarantee.

Coastal Finance will invoke the DLG once a loan has been overdue for 180 days.

The DLG agreement stays in force for 5 years, longer than the longest loan tenor in the portfolio (3 years).

CredBridge publishes on its website, every month within seven working days, the number of portfolios and the amount of each portfolio covered by DLG.

Repayments go directly into Indus Valley Bank's account via UPI or net banking. FlexLine never handles borrower funds.

DLD2025:17(vii).text: vii. RE shall ensure that the reporting in respect of all DLAs on the CIMS portal is completed by June 15, 2025.
DLD2025:17(vii).title: Reporting of DLAs to RBI

DLD2025:19(ii).text: ii. RE shall ensure that any DLG arrangement does not act as a substitute for credit appraisal requirements and robust credit underwriting standards need to be put in place irrespective of the DLG cover.
DLD2025:19(ii).title: Due diligence and other requirements with respect to DLG provider

DLD2025:19(iii).text: iii. Every time a RE enters into or renews a DLG arrangement, it shall obtain adequate information to satisfy itself that the entity extending DLG would be able to honour it. Such information shall, at a minimum, include a declaration from the DLG provider, certified by the statutory auditor of the DLG provider, on the aggregate DLG amount outstanding, the number of RE and the respective number of portfolios against which DLG has been provided. The declaration shall also contain past default rates on similar portfolios.
DLD2025:19(iii).title: Due diligence and other requirements with respect to DLG provider

DLD2025:20(i).text: i. RE shall not enter into DLG arrangements for revolving credit facilities offered through digital lending channel and credit cards as defined under Master Direction – Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022 dated April 21, 2022 .
DLD2025:20(i).title: Restrictions on entering into DLG arrangements

DLD2025:20(ii).text: ii. RE shall not enter into DLG arrangements on the loans which are covered by the credit guarantee schemes administered by trust funds as specified under para 2 of Review of Prudential Norms – Risk Weights for Exposures guaranteed by Credit Guarantee Schemes (CGS) dated September 07, 2022 , as amended from time to time.
DLD2025:20(ii).title: Restrictions on entering into DLG arrangements

DLD2025:20(iii).text: iii. NBFC – P2P shall not enter into DLG arrangements for the loans facilitated over its platform and be guided by para 6(1)(iv) of Master Direction - Non-Banking Financial Company – Peer to Peer Lending Platform (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2017 dated October 04, 2017 , as amended from time to time.
DLD2025:20(iii).title: Restrictions on entering into DLG arrangements

DLD2025:21(i).title: Structure of DLG arrangements

DLD2025:22(i).title: Forms of DLG

DLD2025:23(i).text: i. RE shall ensure that the total amount of DLG cover on any outstanding portfolio which is specified upfront shall not exceed five per cent of the total amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio at any given time. In case of implicit guarantee arrangements, the DLG Provider shall not bear performance risk of more than the equivalent amount of five per cent of the underlying loan portfolio.
DLD2025:23(i).title: Cap on DLG

DLD2025:24(ii).text: ii. The amount of DLG invoked shall not be set off against the underlying individual loans, i.e. the liability of the borrowers in respect of the underlying loan shall remain unaffected.
DLD2025:24(ii).title: Recognition of NPA

DLD2025:24(iv).text: iv. DLG amount once invoked by the RE shall not be reinstated, including through loan recovery.
DLD2025:24(iv).title: Recognition of NPA

DLD2025:26(i).text: i. RE shall invoke DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the loan dues are made good by the borrower before that.
DLD2025:26(i).title: Invocation and tenor of DLG

DLD2025:26(ii).text: ii. The period for which the DLG agreement remains in force shall not be less than the longest tenor of the loan in the underlying loan portfolio.
DLD2025:26(ii).title: Invocation and tenor of DLG

DLD2025:27(i).text: i. RE shall put in place a mechanism to ensure that LSPs with whom they have a DLG arrangement shall publish on their website the total number of portfolios and the respective amount of each portfolio on which DLG has been offered. The name of the RE may or may not be disclosed as part of disclosure under this provision.
DLD2025:27(i).title: Disclosure requirements

DLD2025:27(ii).text: ii. Disclosure under para (i) above shall be made on a monthly basis, with the disclosure for any given month to be provided no later than seven (7) working days following the conclusion of that month.
DLD2025:27(ii).title: Disclosure requirements

DLD2025:5(i).text: i. Digital lending by a RE involving a LSP, shall be carried out under a contractual agreement between the RE and the LSP, which clearly defines the respective roles, rights, and obligations of each party thereto.
DLD2025:5(i).title: Due diligence requirements with respect to LSPs

DLD2025:5(ii).text: ii. RE shall conduct enhanced due diligence before they enter into an agreement with a LSP for digital lending, taking into account LSP’s technical capabilities, robustness of data privacy policies and storage systems, fairness in conduct with borrowers, past records of conduct and ability to comply with all applicable regulations and statutes.
DLD2025:5(ii).title: Due diligence requirements with respect to LSPs

DLD2025:5(v).text: v. RE shall impart necessary guidance to LSP acting as a recovery agent, to discharge their duties responsibly and ensure that LSP complies with the applicable instructions 2 in this regard.
DLD2025:5(v).title: Due diligence requirements with respect to LSPs

DLD2025:6(i).text: i. LSP shall provide a digital view of all the loan offers matching the borrower’s request on the DLA which meets the requirement of the borrower. The name of the unmatched lenders shall also be disclosed in the digital view.
DLD2025:6(i).title: RE-LSP arrangements involving multiple lenders

DLD2025:6(ii).text: ii. While the LSP may adopt any mechanism to match the request of borrowers with the lender (s) to offer a loan, it shall follow a consistent approach for similarly placed borrowers and products. The mechanism adopted by the LSP and any subsequent changes to this mechanism shall be properly documented.
DLD2025:6(ii).title: RE-LSP arrangements involving multiple lenders

DLD2025:6(iii).text: iii. The digital view of loan offers from matching lenders shall include the name (s) of the RE (s) extending the loan offer, amount and tenor of loan, APR, monthly repayment obligation and penal charges (if applicable), in a way which enables the borrower to make a fair comparison between various offers. A link to the KFS shall also be provided in respect of each of the RE.
DLD2025:6(iii).title: RE-LSP arrangements involving multiple lenders

DLD2025:6(iv).text: iv. The content displayed by the LSP shall be unbiased, objective and shall not directly/ indirectly promote or push a product of a particular RE, including the use of dark patterns/deceptive patterns 4 designed to mislead borrowers into choosing a particular loan offer. However, ranking of loan offers based on a publicly pre-disclosed metric for such ranking shall not be construed as promoting a particular product.
DLD2025:6(iv).title: RE-LSP arrangements involving multiple lenders

DLD2025:7(i).text: i. RE shall obtain the necessary information relating to economic profile of the borrower with a view to assessing the borrower’s creditworthiness before extending any loan, including, at a minimum, age, occupation and income details. The same shall be kept on record for audit purposes.
DLD2025:7(i).title: Assessing the borrower’s creditworthiness

DLD2025:7(ii).text: ii. RE shall ensure that there is no automatic increase in credit limit unless an explicit request is received, evaluated and kept on record from the borrower for such increase.
DLD2025:7(ii).title: Assessing the borrower’s creditworthiness

DLD2025:8(i).text: i. RE shall provide a Key Fact Statement (KFS), as per instructions contained in circular no. DOR.STR.REC.13/13.03.00/2024-25 on ‘Key Facts Statement (KFS) for Loans & Advances’ dated April 15, 2024 , as amended from time to time.
DLD2025:8(i).title: Disclosures to borrowers

DLD2025:8(iii).text: iii. RE shall ensure that digitally signed documents 5 (on the letter head of the RE) viz., KFS, summary of loan product, sanction letter, terms and conditions, account statements, privacy policies of the RE / LSP with respect to storage and usage of borrowers’ data, etc. shall automatically flow to the borrower on the registered and verified email/ SMS upon execution of the loan contract/ transactions.
DLD2025:8(iii).title: Disclosures to borrowers

DLD2025:8(iv).title: Disclosures to borrowers

DLD2025:8(v).text: v. In case of a loan default, when a recovery agent is assigned for recovery or there is a change in the recovery agent already assigned, the particulars of such recovery agent authorised to approach the borrower for recovery shall be communicated to the borrower through email/ SMS before the recovery agent contacts the borrower for recovery.
DLD2025:8(v).title: Disclosures to borrowers

DLD2025:9(i).text: i. Disbursement of loan by the RE shall always be made into the bank account of the borrower except for disbursals covered exclusively under statutory or regulatory mandate (of RBI or of any other regulator), flow of money between REs for co-lending transactions 6 and disbursals for specific end use, provided the loan is disbursed directly into the bank account of the end-beneficiary 7 . RE shall ensure that in no case, disbursal is made to a third-party account, including the accounts of LSP, except as provided for in these Directions.
DLD2025:9(i).title: Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment

DLD2025:9(ii).text: ii. RE shall ensure that all loan servicing, repayment, etc. is executed by the borrower directly in the RE’s bank account without any pass-through account/ pool account of any third party, including the accounts of LSP.
DLD2025:9(ii).title: Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment

DLD2025:9(iii).text: iii. The flow of funds between the bank accounts of the borrower and the RE shall not be controlled either directly or indirectly by a third-party, including the LSP.
DLD2025:9(iii).title: Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment

DLD2025:9(iv).text: iv. RE shall ensure that any fees, charges, reimbursements, etc. payable to LSP are paid directly by the RE and are not charged to or collected from the borrowers separately by LSP.
DLD2025:9(iv).title: Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment

DLD2025:9(v).text: v. In case of delinquent loans, RE may deploy physical interface to recover loans in cash, wherever necessary. In order to afford operational flexibility to RE, such transactions are exempted from the requirement of direct repayment of loan in the RE’s bank account. However, any recovery by cash shall be duly reflected in full in the borrower’s account on the same day and RE shall ensure that any fees, charges, etc., payable to LSPs for such recovery are paid directly by the RE and are not charged by LSP to the borrower either directly or indirectly from the recovery proceeds.
DLD2025:9(v).title: Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment

KFS2024:4.text: REs shall provide a KFS to all prospective borrowers to help them take an informed view before executing the loan contract, as per the standardised format given in the Annex A . The KFS shall be written in a language understood by such borrowers. Contents of KFS shall be explained to the borrower and an acknowledgement shall be obtained that he/she has understood the same.

KFS2024:5.text:
Further, the KFS shall be provided with a unique proposal number and shall have a validity period of at least three working days for loans having tenor of seven days or more, and a validity period of one working day for loans having tenor of less than seven days. 1
Explanation
Validity period refers to the period available to the borrower, after being provided the KFS by the RE, to agree to the terms of the loan. The RE shall be bound by the terms of the loan indicated in the KFS, if agreed to by the borrower during the validity period.

KFS2024:6.text: The KFS shall also include a computation sheet of annual percentage rate (APR), and the amortisation schedule of the loan over the loan tenor. APR will include all charges which are levied by the RE. Illustrative examples of calculation of APR and disclosure of repayment schedule for a hypothetical loan are given in Annex B and C respectively .

KFS2024:7.text: Charges recovered from the borrowers by the REs on behalf of third-party service providers on actual basis, such as insurance charges, legal charges etc., shall also form part of the APR and shall be disclosed separately. In all cases wherever the RE is involved in recovering such charges, the receipts and related documents shall be provided to the borrower for each payment, within a reasonable time.

KFS2024:8.text: Any fees, charges, etc. which are not mentioned in the KFS, cannot be charged by the REs to the borrower at any stage during the term of the loan, without explicit consent of the borrower.

KFS2024:9.text: The KFS shall also be included as a summary box to be exhibited as part of the loan agreement.
